name: Belmond Copacabana Palace
positioning: Historic Belmond beachfront hotel on Avenida Atlântica in Rio de Janeiro, with three restaurants grouped around its pool
best_for: Travelers who want a classic hotel close to Copacabana beach
Food lovers who want several restaurants at the hotel

facts.text: The hotel is on Avenida Atlântica, close to Copacabana beach.
The hotel was modeled by French architect and designer Joseph Gire after the great beach hotels of the 19th and early 20th century.
The 1933 film Flying Down to Rio used meticulously recreated sets that mimicked the hotel's facade.
Belmond, then the Orient-Express group, took over the hotel in 1989.
The restaurants are Cipriani (Italian), MEE (Asian fusion) and Pérgula (Brazilian classics).
The spa is in the new annex and offers a grapeseed-oil Harmonia massage.
The concierge desk sorts tickets in advance for the trip up to the Christ the Redeemer statue on Corcovado.
The hotel runs entirely on renewable energy.
There are a number of accessible rooms, and the restaurants are all accessible via ramp.

highlights.text: Three restaurants are grouped around the pool.
The hotel has a rooftop tennis court.
Beach service includes cold face towels and a watering can to cool down burning feet.
Architect Joseph Gire built the hotel in the image of the great Riviera seaside hotels, in particular the Carlton in Cannes.

considerations.text: The Botanical Garden, the Sugarloaf Mountain cable car and the bossa nova bars and restaurants of Ipanema are easily reached by taxi.
WhataHotel notes the busy beachfront location can be crowded during peak times.
WhataHotel notes premium pricing reflecting the luxury positioning.
